2020–2026

Gone but never missed.

May it remain inside museums forever.

Thanks, Amazon Now.

Five years ago, software engineers rushed into AI.

The next big opportunity might be engineers building for healthcare instead.

That thought hit me while listening to Sowmay Jain talk about peptides, weight loss, and why he chose to build Zelta in India.

It wasn't just a healthcare conversation.

It was a roadmap for the next wave of innovation.

One line from the podcast stuck with me:

"If you're below 50, get ready to live to 150."

Whether that prediction comes true or not isn't the point.

The point is that healthcare is shifting from treating diseases to preventing them.

That's exactly what Zelta is building around  science-backed weight loss and metabolic health, using peptide-based therapies under medical supervision rather than promising shortcuts.

Now add AI to the equation.

More than 1 billion people globally are living with obesity, while AI is making it possible to analyze health data, biomarkers, and patient patterns faster than ever before.

As engineers, we've spent the last few years building copilots for code.

The next decade might be about building copilots for human health.

To me, that's a far bigger problem worth solving.

The next generation of impactful startups may not be another coding tool.

They could sit at the intersection of AI, biotechnology, and preventive healthcare.

If you're an engineer starting today...

would you rather build the next AI coding assistant...

or help build the future of preventive healthcare, weight loss, and innovations like peptides?

I'd love to know which future you'd bet your career on.
